channel.title: The Catholic Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Catholic Review (catholicreview.org)

item.title: Mount 2000 attracts more than 1,100 for eucharistic retreat
item.description: Incense rose, voices sang and young hearts were turned toward Christ at Mount 2000, the yearly eucharistic retreat for high schoolers hosted by Mount St. Mary’s Seminary.

item.title: Little Sisters of Poor ask for gifts of a little bling to help others
item.description: This St. Valentine’s Day, the Little Sisters of the Poor at St. Martin’s Home for the Aged in Catonsville are hoping for a ring – but a gem or even a gold or silver necklace would be welcome, too.

item.title: Oklahoma death-row inmate to be executed Feb. 12, unless he’s granted reprieve or stay
item.description: Death-row inmate Kendrick Simpson is to be executed by lethal injection Feb. 12 unless Oklahoma Gov. Kevin Stitt grants him a last-minute reprieve or the U.S. Supreme Court grants a stay.

item.title: Bishop Rhoades calls on Notre Dame to reverse new director’s appointment over abortion advocacy
item.description: An Indiana bishop is urging the University of Notre Dame to halt the appointment of a faculty member, who advocates openly for abortion, as head of one of the school's research centers.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV prays at Vatican’s Lourdes grotto for the sick on World Day of the Sick
item.description: Pope Leo XIV prayed with the sick at the Lourdes grotto in the Vatican Gardens on Feb. 11, asking Our Lady of Lourdes to accompany all those who suffer in the world.

item.title: Carrie Prejean Boller removed from Religious Liberty Commission after antisemitism row
item.description: Carrie Prejean Boller has been removed from the Religious Liberty Commission, its chair, Texas Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick said Feb. 11.

item.title: Catholic advocates speak out as ICE data shows just 14 percent arrested have violent criminal records
item.description: Catholic immigration advocates are speaking out after an internal federal document obtained by CBS News showed most individuals arrested in Trump administration immigration crackdowns over the past year do not have violent criminal records.

item.title: Question Corner: Why is it a problem for the SSPX to ordain new bishops?
item.description: SSPX's proposed episcopal ordinations are a problem because ordaining new bishops without the permission of the pope (technically called a "mandate") is gravely injurious to Christian unity.

item.title: Movie Review: ‘Shelter’
item.description: It takes nearly an hour of gunfire, car chases and flying fists for the plot of "Shelter" (Black Bear) to emerge. That it's another of Jason Statham's pictures in which he plays a brooding loner who eventually avenges old wrongs. Yet the film almost sneers at viewers for expecting exactly what they get.

item.title: Bishop in British Columbia calls for prayer after mass shooting that ‘has traumatized us all’
item.description: On the feast of Our Lady of Lourdes -- the Church's World Day of the Sick -- Bishop Stephen Jensen of Prince George called the people of northern British Columbia to prayer and penance following a mass school shooting that took place midday Feb. 10 in Tumbler Ridge.
